AMZN.rationale: Amazon demonstrates strong fundamental health and accelerating trajectory across its key segments. Q1 2026 results showed 17% revenue growth to $181.5B, with AWS accelerating to 28% YoY growth (fastest in 15 quarters), operating margin expanding to a record 13.1%, and advertising growing 22% YoY. The quarterly trajectory from the quantitative data shows consistent sequential improvement: revenue grew from $155.67B (Q1 2025) to $167.70B (Q2) to $180.17B (Q3), with EPS rising from $1.59 to $1.68 to $1.95. Balance sheet is solid with $369.6B equity and manageable $55.1B debt (debt-to-equity 0.149). However, the $200B capex commitment for 2026 has compressed free cash flow to just $1.2B TTM (down 95% YoY), which is a meaningful constraint. On valuation, the current P/E of 37.6x sits near the top of its 12-month range (28.2-40.9x), having expanded significantly from the 28.3x trough in late March 2026. The stock has rallied ~25% in 30 days, which has moved valuation from clearly attractive to fair-to-slightly-rich territory. The Q1 earnings beat (EPS $2.78 vs $1.64 est, though aided by $16.8B Anthropic gains) and AWS reacceleration provide a near-term positive catalyst that has already been partially priced in with the post-earnings move. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.30 over 90 days). The combination of excellent business trajectory but elevated near-term valuation and massive capex uncertainty yields a mildly-to-moderately attractive score.
